extracted.intended_audience: policymakers, reformers, and students of public finance (readers of political economy)
extracted.subtask_description: Principles and concrete criteria for designing, assessing, and reforming systems of taxation and revenue administration (customs, excise, farms, monopolies), illustrated with historical national examples. Also introductory observations on public revenue and behaviour in pre-commercial societies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Taxes_on_luxuries_are_voluntary_and_convenient
rubrics_metrics.description: Such taxes upon luxuries ... every man’s contribution is altogether voluntary; it being altogether in his power, either to consume, or not to consume, the commodity taxed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Taxes on luxuries are often paid piece-meal, in proportion as contributors purchase the goods; in time and mode of payment they can be the most convenient of taxes. When advanced by merchants or manufacturers they become conflated with price and are less resented. Proper assessment and selection of commodities can minimize complaint.

rubrics_metrics.name: Taxes_on_luxuries_violate_fourth_maxim
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon the whole, such taxes, therefore, are perhaps as agreeable to the three first of the four general maxims concerning taxation, as any other. They offend in every respect against the fourth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although they satisfy convenience, certainty, and perhaps proportionality in some senses, taxes on luxuries offend the unspecified fourth maxim (inequality/equity). The text warns that despite their conveniences they tend to be unequal in final incidence in particular situations (e.g., absentees).

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity_and_precision_in_tax_laws_to_avoid_uncertainty
rubrics_metrics.description: What ever uncertainty there may sometimes be, either in the duties of customs in Great Britain, or in other duties of the same kind in other countries, it cannot arise from the nature of those duties, but from the inaccurate or unskilful manner in which the law that imposes them is expressed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tax laws should be drafted with precision so that obligations (what, how much, when) are certain; uncertainty is a drafting problem, not intrinsic to customs/excise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collection_costs_reduce_net_yield
rubrics_metrics.description: The levying of such taxes, even when imposed in the most judicious manner, requires a great number of custom-house and excise officers, whose salaries and perquisites are a real tax upon the people, which brings nothing into the treasury of the state.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate taxes net of collection costs (salaries, perquisites, bounties/drawbacks). Example: 1775 gross excise ~£5.5m, neat ~£4.98m; customs levied at >10% expense in salaries and potentially 20–30% when perquisites counted. Policy implication: prefer collection methods and scopes that minimize administration waste.

rubrics_metrics.name: Taxes_discourage_production_and_alter_industry_direction
rubrics_metrics.description: Such taxes necessarily occasion some obstruction or discouragement to certain branches of industry. As they always raise the price of the commodity taxed, they so far discourage its consumption, and consequently its production... All taxes upon consumable commodities, therefore, tend to reduce the quantity of productive labour below what it otherwise would be ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess taxes by their effect on incentives and the 'natural direction' of national industry; consider substitution effects (imported vs domestic goods) and secondary impacts on unrelated industries (examples: wine, Birmingham hardware).

rubrics_metrics.name: High_taxes_encourage_smuggling_and_harsh_enforcement
rubrics_metrics.description: The hope of evading such taxes by smuggling, gives frequent occasion to forfeitures and other penalties, which entirely ruin the smuggler... In those corrupted governments ... not many people are scrupulous about smuggling...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High rates plus perception of misapplied public revenue increase smuggling. Enforcement then becomes severe, producing social costs (forfeitures, ruined capital) and encourages hardened criminality; set rates and enforcement to limit profitable smuggling and avoid unjustly ruinous penalties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vexation_from_frequent_inspections_is_a_cost
rubrics_metrics.description: Such taxes, by subjecting at least the dealers in the taxed commodities, to the frequent visits and odious examination of the tax-gatherers, expose them sometimes ... to some degree of oppression, and always to much trouble and vexation...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider non-monetary costs (vexation, lost time) imposed by excise/customs inspections; excise tends to be more intrusive than customs because dealers face continual visits. These intangible burdens lower public acceptance and can be valued as equivalent to expense people would pay to avoid them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid_repeated_sale_taxes_like_alcavala
rubrics_metrics.description: In consequence of the notion, that duties upon consumable goods were taxes upon the profits of merchants, those duties have, in some countries, been repeated upon every successive sale of the goods. The famous alcavala of Spain ... repeated every time the property is sold.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Taxes repeated on each sale (turnover taxes) require massive administrative oversight, inhibit production for distant sale, and can ruin manufactures and agriculture (Spanish example). Prefer single-point taxation rather than cumulative levies on successive turnovers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uniformity_of_internal_taxation_promotes_free_inland_commerce
rubrics_metrics.description: The uniform system of taxation ... leaves the interior commerce of the country, the inland and coasting trade, almost entirely free... This freedom of interior commerce ... is perhaps one of the principal causes of the prosperity of Great Britain.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy aim: uniform internal taxes to remove checkpoints/permits/let-passes. Extending such uniformity to dependent territories (Ireland, plantations) would likely enhance overall prosperity and market size.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fragmented_provincial_revenue_laws_multiply_restraints_and_officers
rubrics_metrics.description: The different revenue laws which take place in the different provinces, require a multitude of revenue officers to surround, not only the frontiers of the kingdom, but those of almost each particular province ... to the no small interruption of the interior commerce of the country.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple overlapping provincial tariffs, exemptions, and special taxes (gabelles, aides, traites) create administrative bloat and obstruct internal trade; reform requires harmonization across subjurisdictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Government_administration_preferred_to_farming_revenue
rubrics_metrics.description: The best and most frugal way of levying a tax can never be by farm ... Government, by establishing an administration under their own immediate inspection, ... might at least save this profit, which is almost always exorbitant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Farming revenue concentrates collection in few wealthy operators who extract profit, reduce competition, and incentivize harsh laws; prefer state-run administration accountable to government to reduce waste and excessive private profits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revenue_farmers_incentivize_severe_laws_and_corruption
rubrics_metrics.description: The farmers of the public revenue never find the laws too severe, which punish any attempt to evade the payment of a tax... The revenue laws, therefore, become gradually more and more severe.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beware that private revenue farmers prioritize rent recovery and their own security, lobbying for harsher laws and severe enforcement that may be socially destructive; institutional arrangement matters for law severity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Farming_plus_monopoly_compounds_public_burden
rubrics_metrics.description: A tax is sometimes not only farmed for a certain rent, but the farmer has, besides, the monopoly of the commodity taxed... the profit of the farmer, and the still more exorbitant one of the monopolist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combining farmed collection with monopoly supply (example: salt, tobacco) produces double exploitation, huge incentives to smuggle, and brutal enforcement (galleys, gibbet). Avoid creating monopoly-farm structures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer_uniform_indirect_taxes_over_localized_excises
rubrics_metrics.description: Secondly, by rendering the gabelle, the aides, the traites, the taxes upon tobacco, all the different customs and excises, uniform in all the different parts of the kingdom, those taxes might be levied at much less expense, and the interior commerce of the kingdom might be rendered as free as that of England.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Harmonize indirect taxes across regions to reduce collection costs and commercial friction; uniformity reduces number of officers and borders within a state.

rubrics_metrics.name: Replace_inequitable_direct_taxes_with_broad_land-like_tax
rubrics_metrics.description: First, by abolishing the taille and the capitation, and by increasing the number of the vingtiemes, so as to produce an additional revenue equal to the amount of those other taxes, the revenue of the crown might be preserved ... the superior ranks of people might not be more burdened than they are at present.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy reform: substitute arbitrary direct levies (taille, capitation) with a broader, more regular tax (vingtieme akin to land tax) to reduce inequities and collection vexations; expect opposition from privileged interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tariffs_on_raw_materials_harm_manufacturing
rubrics_metrics.description: The British taxes which bear hardest on manufactures, are some duties upon the importation of raw materials, particularly upon that of raw silk.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate import duties not only on finished goods but on inputs; taxes on raw materials reduce manufacturers' competitiveness and can damage domestic industries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Taxes_on_necessaries_are_most_burdensome_but_may_be_necessary
rubrics_metrics.description: The taxes upon the necessaries of life are inconsiderable in Great Britain... After all the proper subjects of taxation have been exhausted, if the exigencies of the state still continue to require new taxes, they must be imposed upon improper ones. The taxes upon the necessaries of life, therefore, may be no impeachment of the wisdom of that republic...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Taxes on necessities fall heaviest and can ruin manufacturers/fisheries (Holland example). They should be avoided where possible but may be reluctantly imposed when all other taxable bases are exhausted (e.g., war debts, extraordinary state expenses).

rubrics_metrics.name: Extend_internal_uniformity_to_dependant_territories_for_growth
rubrics_metrics.description: If the same freedom in consequence of the same uniformity, could be extended to Ireland and the plantations, both the grandeur of the state, and the prosperity of every part of the empire, would probably be still greater than at present.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider broader political-economic benefits of extending internal tax uniformity to dependent or colonial territories to expand domestic market and national prosperity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public_revenue_in_pre-commercial_societies_equals_command_of_necessaries
rubrics_metrics.description: In that rude state of society ... a large revenue may at all times be said to consist in the command of a large quantity of the necessaries of life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When commerce and manufactures are underdeveloped, revenue and wealth are embodied in consumables (corn, cattle, raw materials). Policy and debt instruments should be interpreted in light of the economic structure: limited markets mean the rich sustain dependents and hoard savings rather than exchange widely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Social_behaviour_and_saving_affect_public_debt_dynamics
rubrics_metrics.description: Among our feudal ancestors, the long time during which estates used to continue in the same family, sufficiently demonstrates the general disposition of people to live within their income... Some part of this money, perhaps, they spent ... but some part of it they seem commonly to have hoarded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Historical social norms (living within income, hoarding) influence capital accumulation and thus the state's ability to raise or service public debt; public-debt analysis should account for saving behaviour and limited outlets for expenditure in less commercial economies.
